warnings.why: Kiribati is a collection of low-lying coral atolls with poor soil quality, making the reported 39.5% permanent cropland figure highly implausible compared to its actual agricultural capacity.
Similar to Kiribati, the Marshall Islands consist of atolls with limited soil depth and fertility, making a 37.4% permanent cropland figure inconsistent with its geography.
The 24.3% figure is significantly higher than typical agricultural data for these islands, likely misclassifying wild vegetation or forest cover as permanent cropland.

policy: model memory is advisory; unsupported suspicions cannot overrule official data
